A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LDAdam research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are available and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GLUE and GSM8K fine-tuning results, C4 pre-training results, error-feedback ablations, and memory/runtime measurements in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains original fine-tuning and pre-training experiments, revises their reported results, and adds rank-sensitivity and efficiency measurements in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The projection-aware moment updates, subspace adaptation, generalized error feedback, and analytical normalization remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves the independent gradient-projection calculation between two groups of steps without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate language understanding on GLUE, mathematical reasoning fine-tuning on GSM8K, and language-model pre-training on C4. Llama 1.3B experiments already appear in v1. The added rank sweeps vary configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The main accuracy/perplexity comparator sets remain unchanged. However, the norm diagnostic replaces its stated Adam gradient reference with LDAdam no-EF gradients (v1 Figure 2 versus v4 Figure 5). v4 also distinguishes retained-gradient GaLore in the analytical comparison of Table 1 and adds an SGD memory reference in Figure 3.

E3.justification: The reported Llama 1.3B pre-training learning rate changes from 1e-3 to 5e-4, confirmed in the main text and hyperparameter tables. New rank analyses specify a fixed 5e-4 learning rate for the first 10,000 optimization steps and microbatch size 1 for throughput measurements. These are localized protocol revisions and additions.

E4.justification: v1 already contains error-feedback ablations and selected low/high-rank comparisons. v4 substantially expands sensitivity analysis with six ranks for loss/perplexity in Figure 4 and nine ranks for throughput/memory in Figure 3, directly examining the compression-quality-cost tradeoff. The existing buffer-norm diagnostic is also revised.

E5.justification: Both versions report GLUE averages and standard deviations over three seeds, with the latter moving from Table 7 to Table 8. The standard-deviation values change, but the repeated-run and uncertainty-reporting practices do not.

E6.justification: The quantitative record is substantially expanded by the rank-dependent quality and resource results, alongside revisions throughout the LDAdam/no-EF benchmark results. For example, LDAdam's GLUE average changes from 86.43 to 86.48 and GSM8K rank-512 accuracy from 36.70 to 35.86. Llama 1.3B Adam/LDAdam perplexities change from 16.52/15.81 to 14.86/14.09 under the changed learning rate, so these are not same-setting gains. Appendix memory, runtime, standard-deviation, and norm results also change.

T1.justification: v4 adds symbolic operation-count estimates for individual optimizer stages and an orthogonalization complexity expression in Appendix B.1/Table 5. The convergence assumptions, theorem statements, lemmas, and complete Appendix E proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: memory-efficient adaptive optimization through projection-aware updates and generalized error feedback, convergence guarantees, and competitive language-model training performance. Added analyses support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds an explicit isotropy interpretation in Appendix A, expands discussion of bounded-gradient assumptions, and qualifies GaLore's gradient-accumulation versus memory tradeoff. It removes v1's explicit statement that distributed training would require technical algorithm changes. The principal error-feedback and compression-regularization interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v4 identifies the GaLore implementation used and explains the relevant PyTorch gradient hooks in Appendix D. It also specifies runtime microbatch sizes of 128 for Llama 350M and 64 for Llama 1.3B, replacing the earlier generic accumulation description. The LDAdam code link was already present in v1; its move into the abstract is not new availability.

R1.justification: The brief justification of standard assumptions becomes a more detailed comparison with strong-growth, bounded-noise, and ADOPT analyses, adding references including Li et al. (2023), Hong and Lin (2024), and Taniguchi et al. (2024). References supporting implicit regularization and implementation discussion are also added. The overall positioning against GaLore remains stable.

P1.justification: v4 makes targeted prose edits, separates memory/runtime and experiments into top-level sections, and promotes the existing impact statement to an Ethics Statement. Appendices B and D gain clearer subsection organization. Most of the method, introduction, and convergence narrative is retained.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands the visual presentation with three new paired figures: a wall-clock view of pre-training, rank-dependent resource measurements, and rank sensitivity. It adds operation-count Table 5 and a retained-gradient GaLore column in Table 1. The former Figure 2 becomes a redrawn Figure 5 with a changed comparator legend and norm scale.

improvement.justification: The added rank-sensitivity and resource analyses make the practical quality-memory-runtime tradeoff better supported, while implementation disclosures improve reproducibility. These gains refine a paper whose core method, proofs, and benchmark coverage were already present. Some new presentation inconsistencies limit the improvement: v4 Figure 2 labels the Llama 1.3B curve as rank 8, whereas the main text and Figure 1 specify rank 16.
